requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

findings.claim: The new filter in the constructor drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the compilation, including ones about types declared in that compilation. On a positional record parameter, `[property: Key(null)]` declares a property whose declaring syntax is a ParameterSyntax, not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` therefore returns null, the diagnostic gets Location.None, and `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` discards the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull error. Base crashed with an InvalidCastException at this point; head now reports nothing, so an invalid source-declared [MessagePackObject] passes analysis silently.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.PositionalRecordNullKeyDiagnosticTests.NullKeyOnPositionalRecordPropertyIsStillReported. It runs all analyzers on `[MessagePackObject] public partial record Cmd([property: Key(null)] string Scope);` and expects the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic. On head no such diagnostic is reported.

findings.claim: The test 'ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember' only asserts no diagnostics; it does not distinguish the MemberNeedsKey FirstOrDefault change (line 1077) from the wrapper filter. With the wrapper in place, reverting the FirstOrDefault()?. change would still be caught only if an exception occurs. Note that Diagnostic.Create with a null location is fine, so the hunk could be mutated without failing. Also, the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path (line 985) has no test at all: nothing in the diff exercises a metadata property with a [Key]-attribute having null int and string keys.

hunches.claim: The reporter names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites. The diff changes only two of them (old 982 and 1074); the earlier one (reported near line 735, inside GetObjectInfo) is untouched. The new reporting filter cannot prevent a crash there, because Diagnostic.Create arguments (or any indexing outside `?.Invoke`) are evaluated before the filter runs. The generator likely passes no reportDiagnostic callback; if so, it never evaluates the arguments guarded by `?.Invoke`, and its CS8785 crash must come from an unguarded site such as this remaining one. The generator would then still crash on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile the requirement's `lib` (`[MessagePackObject] public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);`) to a MetadataReference via CSharpCompilation.Emit. Then run CSharpGeneratorDriver with MessagePackGenerator, plus compilation.WithAnalyzers(all analyzers), over `app` (Cmd with `[Key(1)] public Item<int> Member`) and a `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class R {}`. Assert no CS8785, no AD0001, and that a resolver source is generated. Repeat with a plain `struct Item<T>`.

hunches.claim: The constructor now wraps reportDiagnostic in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which drops every diagnostic whose Location is not in source or not in this compilation. Any diagnostic previously reported with Location.None (null location resolves to None) is now silently suppressed. Examples are MsgPack004 on a member inherited from a base type in a referenced assembly, and diagnostics whose syntax lookup returns null. Users who relied on these errors (MsgPack003/004/005 are Errors) stop seeing them. That is a behavior change beyond the crash fix, and the requirement asked only that the crash be avoided.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test: a [MessagePackObject] class in the compiling assembly derives from a base class in a referenced assembly. The base has a public property without [Key]. Run with base and head builds and compare the MsgPack004 diagnostic. If head reports nothing where base reported a diagnostic with Location.None, the finding is confirmed. Also repeat with a metadata-only member that previously produced a location-less error.

hunches.claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper (ReportIfLocatedInCompilation) drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a source tree of the current compilation, including Location.None. Diagnostics with no location, or located in generated or other trees, are silently suppressed. This could hide diagnostics that protect against insecure or unsupported configurations (e.g. MsgPack004/005 on a member with null or metadata location). In the same-assembly case where a location lookup returns null (e.g. the property is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax), the diagnostic is now discarded rather than reported. The security impact is limited because it only applies to compile-time diagnostics and the dropped cases involve referenced-assembly types, which L8 says are deliberately not analysed.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an analyzer test with a [MessagePackObject] type in the compilation whose member has a diagnostic location that is null or not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax (e.g. a field or primary-constructor-derived property with BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull). Assert the diagnostic is still reported, and compare against base-built behavior.

hunches.claim: The reportDiagnostic wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of this compilation, for all diagnostic paths and not only the metadata ones. The behaviour change is broad. Diagnostics created with a null or None location in the compilation's own types (e.g. MemberNeedsKey with a null location from the FirstOrDefault change) are now silently suppressed instead of reported. The tests only cover metadata types and do not check that source-declared diagnostics still fire.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests for MsgPack003/004/005 and similar on same-assembly types. Also add a test where a source-declared type inherits an unkeyed public member from a base type in a referenced assembly and expect MsgPack004, or an explicit decision to suppress it.

hunches.claim: The key diagnostic filter (ReportIfLocatedInCompilation) that drops all diagnostics whose location is not in the compilation has no negative test. Tests only assert no diagnostics. If the filter were removed or inverted, a metadata type would yield Location.None diagnostics, which are not dropped. The tests use well-formed metadata types, so diagnostics are only suppressed, never shown to be correctly reported for source types. No test checks that real diagnostics (MsgPack004 on a source type) are still reported after the wrapper is added, so a filter that always drops would survive.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1445 negate-condition: if (diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(...)) -> if (false); expected to survive because every new test asserts zero diagnostics, so dropping all diagnostics passes. Existing analyzer tests (MsgPack003/004) may kill it; confirm by running them.

hunches.claim: The first two tests (struct and record struct) only check the absence of warnings and the presence of the resolver hint name. They never check that the resolver content or that Item<int> is handled consistently; also SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck is set, so the generated output is not verified. The generated resolver could be wrong or empty and the tests would still pass.

receipt_plan.detail: tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/GenericsFormatterTests.cs:620 remove-guard: TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck stays; mutate the generator so the resolver is emitted empty but under the same hint name; expected to survive because only the HintName is asserted via Assert.Contains.

hunches.claim: The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic now passes a null location when FirstOrDefault() finds no syntax. Diagnostic.Create with a null location becomes Location.None, and the new filter then drops it. For metadata members the diagnostic is therefore lost, with no error and no fallback to the derived type's identifier. For inherited members without [Key] this removes an error-level MsgPack004 that existed before whenever the location was valid. This is only a hunch from reading the code.

receipt_plan.detail: Read TypeCollector.cs around line 1077 and ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. Confirm that a null location becomes Location.None, which is not IsInSource, so the diagnostic is discarded.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: The new README and MsgPack004 doc text says diagnostics for referenced-assembly types are deliberately left to the defining assembly. This matches ledger L8, which records that metadata types are not analysed. The ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter that drops diagnostics without a source location in this compilation is consistent with that. It is recorded as checked, not as a defect.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and a missing diagnostic for such a type is not a defect. The filter, the docs and the unkeyed-member test follow this.
